Global Regulatory Compliance Lead

About Aspora

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.

We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.

About the Role

People build lives across borders, and their finances should move with them. We’re building Aspora for the global diaspora, starting with Indians abroad. Regulation sits at the centre of that ambition. This role exists to turn a complex set of requirements into a practical way to build and run the business. One global framework, local differences only where the law needs them, and decisions made by clear frameworks rather than daily escalations.

You’ll lead licensing, regulator engagement, product advice, safeguarding oversight, customer protection and operational resilience. You’ll report to our COO, working alongside our Global MLRO. You’ll partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and local compliance owners to turn requirements into working controls. You’ll own the regulatory calls on launches, changes and the commitments we make to regulators.

Who You Are

You don’t see regulation as a reason to say no, or as something to work around. You know a hard boundary from a choice, and your depth goes well beyond AML or licensing paperwork.

  • You’ve scaled fintechs before. You’ve helped a payments, remittance or e-money business grow, in house or as a consultant, and can show what you changed.

  • You turn expertise into execution. You’ve translated payments and e-money requirements into customer journeys, controls and processes, with fewer failures and less friction to show for it.

  • You get permissions over the line. You’ve owned licensing or variation work and regulatory reporting, and kept applications, governance and operating reality consistent throughout.

  • You speak regulator fluently, and you’ve been tested. You’ve handled supervisory questions, inspections or a hard remediation, made sound calls under pressure and stayed until it was fixed.

  • You’ve set standards at HQ level. You’ve built shared standards across markets and distributed teams, and you know where local law needs a difference and where duplication is habit.

  • You’ve seen controls work in practice. You go deep on UK payments, e-money, safeguarding and customer protection, and you’ve followed gaps through to a verified fix.

  • You’re on the way up. Your career shows quick progression, growing ownership and real depth. We’ll judge the work you’ve done, not the title you hold.

Most importantly, you want to build a global regulatory framework from the ground up and see it work in practice.

What You’ll Own

This is a role with a genuinely global mandate, with UK payments and e-money regulation as the depth anchor.

  • Own licensing and regulator engagement. Lead permissions, perimeter analysis, applications and variations, with accurate filings and a clear register of every commitment we make.

  • Shape products before they launch. Assess launches and changes against UK PSRs, EMRs and FCA rules, and turn horizon scanning into owned implementation plans.

  • Hold safeguarding to a high standard. Challenge the design, test the evidence and keep us audit ready, partnering with Finance on reconciliations and governance.

  • Make customer protection measurable. Drive Consumer Duty, fair value, vulnerable customers, complaints and partner oversight, using outcome data to spot harm and assign action.

  • Own the regulatory view on resilience. Partner with operations and technology owners on service mapping, testing and outsourcing oversight, and own the incident reporting decisions.

  • Build one global framework. Set shared standards across markets, add local differences only where law requires them, and bring in local expertise where it’s needed.

What you build here will shape where Aspora can launch, how quickly we get there, and how much regulators trust us along the way.

Why Aspora

  • Define the global regulatory compliance framework for a borderless financial platform, from first principles.

  • Work directly with our COO and Global MLRO, and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance and Operations.

  • Set the standard for how a regulated fintech scales across multiple jurisdictions without losing pace.

  • Own licensing, product advice, safeguarding oversight and customer protection from day one, not a narrow slice of compliance.

  • Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

jobs.description:
AI Implementation Intern

About MakiPeople

Maki builds AI agents that help large companies hire faster and better, from screening to assessment to candidate engagement. Global enterprises use Maki to run hiring at scale, giving recruiters time back and candidates a smoother experience. With offices in Paris and London, we are now accelerating in New York. As an intern on our Implementation team, you will work on live customer rollouts and see how AI is deployed inside large organizations. You will get real responsibility and close mentorship from day one.

 

About the Implementation team
You will be joining our Implementation team and will be working with our UE-based team, collaborating across EMEA and Asia, and alongside both our Implementation Managers (IMs) and our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs). You will also have the chance to collaborate with everyone at Maki.
Most of the Implementation team’s efforts are currently focused on onboarding our (many) new clients, making sure they can use Maki to its fullest potential and that the impact we promise is delivered. Because we support large Enterprise companies, this is large-scale project management and change management, built hand-in-hand with our clients.

About your mission
As an Implementation Intern, you will support our Implementation Managers and Forward Deployed Engineers with a variety of operational tasks while actively contributing to live client projects. Your role is multi-faceted and cuts across several parts of the customer journey, with a strong focus on configuration, testing and cross-team collaboration.


Your key responsibilities:

  • Support client implementation: Help define candidate journeys, monitor impact, and ensure smooth onboarding.

  • AI agent configuration: Configure Maki’s AI agents to match each client’s needs and hiring processes.

  • AI agent testing: Run structured testing loops on the agents, analyze results, and iterate with the IMs and FDEs until the agents perform as intended.

  • Cross-team collaboration: Work with internal teams at Maki, including Science, Tech, Ops and Customer Success Managers, to align configuration with client needs.

  • Process optimization: Design and refine key processes to monitor implementations efficiently using ClickUp (our Implementation and Success internal tool).

  • Contribute to strategic projects: Work on initiatives that support large-scale projects and change management for our enterprise clients.



What we’re looking for

  • Sharp attention to detail and strong problem-solving skills: You spot what others miss and enjoy getting to the root of an issue.

  • Excellent English, spoken and written: You communicate clearly and concisely and can adapt to colleagues or clients.

  • Startup energy: You thrive in a fast-paced environment where priorities move quickly.

  • Ownership and an extra-mile mindset: You take responsibility for outcomes and go beyond what is asked.

  • Analytical thinking: You can spot patterns in test results, summarize them, and recommend clear next steps.

  • Strong project organization: You keep multiple workstreams moving with clear trackers and timely follow-ups.

  • Must have an internship agreement (convention de stage) with a French university



Bonus points if you have

  • Languages: You speak more than one language. Maki works with global clients, so this is always a plus.

  • Tools we use every day: You have used ClickUp, Lovable, Claude, Cursor or Linear, or you pick up new tools quickly.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Success Manager – Usage & Adoption
jobs.description:
Senior Customer Success Manager – Usage & Adoption

Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides.

Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, 2 choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission.

Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé.

⚡ Notre équipe Customer Success

L’équipe Customer Success accompagne les établissements de santé une fois nos solutions déployées.

Sa mission : faire en sorte que les professionnels de santé utilisent Lifen au bon niveau, dans la durée, et qu’ils en tirent un bénéfice concret au quotidien.

Ce poste n’est pas un rôle d’Account Manager ou de CSM orienté renouvellement, upsell ou gestion contractuelle. Il ne s’agit pas non plus de piloter le déploiement technique ou de prendre en charge le support.

Ton terrain de jeu commence une fois les solutions en place : comprendre comment elles sont réellement utilisées, identifier ce qui limite leur adoption et construire les actions permettant de faire évoluer durablement les usages.

Tu rejoindras l’équipe en charge des établissements publics les plus stratégiques. Ton portefeuille regroupera des organisations aux tailles, configurations, pratiques et contraintes très différentes. Tu devras être capable de comprendre rapidement ce qui se passe chez chaque client, de distinguer les symptômes des causes et de mobiliser les bons leviers, côté client comme chez Lifen.

Le poste couvre les trois produits Lifen Care déjà déployés chez nos clients.

Ta mission peut se résumer simplement : comprendre pourquoi nos solutions ne sont pas encore utilisées à leur plein potentiel dans certains établissements et faire évoluer durablement ces usages.

🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous

  • Prendre en main un portefeuille d’environ 35 hôpitaux et cliniques et construire, pour chacun, une lecture précise des usages, des interlocuteurs clés, du contexte organisationnel, des points de blocage et des opportunités.

  • Construire une véritable stratégie de portefeuille. Tu ne pourras pas accompagner 35 établissements avec le même niveau d’intensité : à toi d’identifier où ton intervention aura le plus d’impact, quels comptes nécessitent une attention immédiate et lesquels peuvent être accompagnés de manière plus scalable.

  • Diagnostiquer les freins à l’adoption à partir des données d’usage, des échanges avec les clients et de ta compréhension de leur environnement. Une baisse d’usage peut avoir des causes très différentes : configuration, organisation, processus internes, compréhension du produit, changement d’interlocuteur ou inadéquation entre l’usage réel et l’objectif initial.

  • Transformer ce diagnostic en plans d’action concrets. Selon les situations, cela pourra passer par de la formation, une évolution des pratiques, une modification de configuration, la mobilisation de nouveaux interlocuteurs ou un travail avec nos équipes Produit, Support ou Customer Operations.

  • Accompagner les premières phases d’usage après le déploiement afin de rapprocher progressivement l’usage réel des objectifs définis avec le client. La formation fait partie des leviers possibles, mais ton rôle est avant tout de comprendre quel levier activer et pourquoi.

  • Utiliser les données disponibles pour repérer les signaux faibles et prioriser tes actions : baisse d’usage, adoption partielle, comportement atypique, insatisfaction, évolution de l’organisation ou opportunité d’étendre un usage existant.

  • Animer la relation avec les référents, chefs de projet et équipes opérationnelles côté client. Cela passe par des échanges réguliers à distance et environ un à deux déplacements par mois dans les établissements.

  • Faire avancer des sujets qui nécessitent plusieurs équipes sans avoir nécessairement d’autorité directe sur elles. Tu documentes le problème, fais émerger les priorités et coordonnes les équipes Customer Operations, Produit, Support, Product Marketing ou commerciales lorsque leur intervention est nécessaire.

  • Mesurer l’effet des actions engagées. Un plan d’action n’est pas terminé lorsqu’il est lancé : tu vérifies si les usages évoluent réellement et ajustes ton approche en conséquence.

  • Améliorer les outils et méthodes de l’équipe : tableaux de suivi, segmentation du portefeuille, campagnes d’accompagnement, pratiques de formation, indicateurs ou partage structuré des retours terrain.

⭐️ Ce que nous recherchons

Must-have

  • Tu as une expérience significative dans la gestion de clients ou d’organisations complexes et tu as déjà exercé un rôle avec un niveau élevé d’autonomie. Nous recherchons un profil senior, capable de prendre en charge un portefeuille rapidement et de construire sa propre approche.

  • Tu as déjà géré de façon autonome un portefeuille conséquent, idéalement composé d’au moins une vingtaine de comptes significatifs, et tu sais arbitrer où investir ton temps plutôt que traiter chaque client de manière identique.

  • Tu as déjà été directement responsable de l’adoption, de la réussite client ou de l’amélioration des usages d’un produit ou d’une solution. Tu ne te limites pas au suivi relationnel ou commercial d’un portefeuille.

  • Tu es à l’aise avec des données d’usage produit. Tu sais passer d’un tableau de bord ou d’un ensemble d’indicateurs à des hypothèses, identifier les situations à investiguer et confronter les données à ce que tu observes sur le terrain.

  • Tu sais travailler sur des problèmes qui ne sont pas immédiatement formulés. À partir d’un signal (baisse d’usage, insatisfaction, faible adoption) tu sais mener le diagnostic, distinguer les causes possibles et choisir une approche adaptée.

  • Face à des organisations, des outils et des processus différents, tu sais apporter du conseil sur les dimensions fonctionnelles, organisationnelles et techniques d’un usage.

  • Tu sais cadrer un plan d’action, le prioriser, obtenir l’implication des interlocuteurs nécessaires et suivre son effet dans le temps jusqu’à constater un changement concret.

  • Tu sais faire avancer un sujet sans nécessairement avoir d’autorité directe sur les personnes impliquées. Tu es capable de documenter un problème, défendre une priorité et obtenir des décisions auprès de plusieurs équipes.

Nice-to-have

  • Tu connais l’environnement hospitalier, les contraintes des établissements de santé ou les grands programmes de transformation numérique du secteur.

  • Tu as travaillé dans le SaaS, la fintech, les logiciels métiers ou un environnement réglementé où la rigueur opérationnelle compte autant que la qualité de la relation client.

  • Ton intitulé de poste précédent importe peu : CSM, consultant·e, chef·fe de projet ou autre. En revanche, tu as déjà été responsable de faire évoluer durablement les usages d’un produit ou d’une solution chez des clients complexes.

  • Tu as déjà contribué à faire évoluer des tableaux de bord, des indicateurs, une segmentation client ou des pratiques d’accompagnement.

Soft skills

Tu es à l’aise dans des situations où ni le problème ni la solution ne sont immédiatement évidents.

Tu sais avancer avec des informations incomplètes, formuler des hypothèses, décider où investir ton temps et expliquer tes arbitrages. Tu poses les bonnes questions, prends des initiatives réfléchies et assumes tes choix.

Tu es capable de challenger un client ou une équipe interne lorsque tu penses qu’une autre approche produira davantage d’impact, tout en maintenant une relation constructive.

Tu es fiable et autonome : tu sais faire avancer un sujet, alerter lorsqu’il est bloqué et prioriser dans un portefeuille dense. Avec les équipes hospitalières comme en interne, tu communiques avec clarté, écoute et pédagogie.

Nos valeurs

  • Embrace Complexity — Tu ne t’arrêtes pas au premier symptôme. Tu explores un contexte client parfois complexe, tu comprends ce qui bloque réellement et tu construis un chemin praticable avec les bonnes personnes.

  • Bienveillance — Tu crées une relation de confiance avec les clients et les équipes internes. Tu donnes du feedback factuel, tu écoutes et tu sais challenger ou désamorcer les tensions sans éviter les sujets difficiles.

  • Real Impact — Tu privilégies les actions qui produisent un changement mesurable dans les usages et améliorent réellement l’expérience des professionnels de santé et la santé de ton portefeuille.

👥 Process de recrutement

  1. Échange avec Laura, Talent Acquisition - 30 min. Un premier échange pour comprendre ton parcours, tes attentes et ta motivation pour le poste.

  2. Entretien avec Pierre, Hiring Manager - 60 min. Une première rencontre avec ton potentiel futur manager qui approfondira ton expérience de gestion de portefeuille, ton rapport aux données et ta façon de faire avancer des plans d’action avec des clients et plusieurs équipes internes.

  3. Étude de cas avec Pierre et un membre de l’équipe CS - 90 min. Tu recevras le cas quelques jours avant la restitution. L’objectif est de comprendre ton raisonnement, ta capacité à structurer une recommandation et ta manière de piloter un sujet client de bout en bout.

  4. Entretien Cultural Alignement avec Raphaël, VP ops - 30 min. Cet échange permet de discuter de ta façon de travailler, de ta collaboration avec les autres équipes et de revenir sur d’éventuels sujets à approfondir après les premières étapes.

Nous nous engageons à te faire un retour dans les 72 heures suivant chaque étape.

 

Informations pratiques : poste en CDI, basé idéalement à Paris mais ouvert France entière avec venue régulière à Paris. Des déplacements en établissements sont à prévoir, en moyenne une à deux fois par mois.

Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications (m/w/d) 80-100%

About Traila

At Traila, we are dedicated to shaping the future of rail transport through cutting-edge technology. Since our founding in 2017, we have been driven by a passion for sustainability and excellence. We believe that rail transport is a cornerstone of a greener future, and our mission is to make it quieter, more efficient, and more reliable.

Our talented team is at the heart of this mission, and we are looking for an Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications to join us in developing robust software solutions that operate reliably in real-world railway environments.

What you will do

- Industrial Software Development: Design, implement and maintain robust application software for industrial and railway products using C++, C#, Python or comparable technologies.

- Application & System Integration: Translate system and operational requirements into practical software functionality and integrate software with real hardware and physical systems.

- Hardware & Device Interfaces: Integrate sensors, actuators, controllers, DAQ systems and other industrial devices.

- Communication Protocols: Implement and troubleshoot interfaces such as CAN/CANopen, EtherCAT, TCP/IP and other industrial or vehicle communication protocols.

- Controls & Application Logic: Implement state machines, operational logic, control functionality and system behaviour required by the application.

- Commissioning & Field Support: Support installation, commissioning and field testing on prototypes, test systems and rail vehicles, including travel to customer and test sites when required.

- Diagnostics & Troubleshooting: Analyse logs, interfaces and system behaviour to identify root causes and solve software and integration issues efficiently.

- Testing & Validation: Develop unit, integration and system-level tests and contribute to HIL/SIL or other validation activities where relevant.

- Software Architecture, Quality & Controlled Releases: Own software architecture and release discipline, including configuration and version control, code reviews, test evidence and controlled software releases.

- Product Cybersecurity: Own threat assessment, secure access and software updates, vulnerability handling and lifecycle security maintenance; coordinate specialist security reviews and work with Systems/RAMS on vehicle interfaces and safety consequences.

- Technical Guidance & Mentoring: Review implementations, share practical software-engineering practices and mentor colleagues to strengthen consistency, maintainability and technical ownership across the team.

- Tools & Data: Develop tools for configuration, testing, diagnostics, data acquisition and analysis that support engineering and field activities.

- Documentation & Continuous Improvement: Maintain clear software and interface documentation and improve existing code as Traila products mature from development into deployed systems.

What you bring

- Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical technical experience.

- Hands-on professional software-development experience in an industrial, automation, automotive, machinery or comparable technical environment.

- Proven professional railway software experience, including products released and maintained in service.

- Strong practical programming skills in C++, C#, Python or a comparable industrial software stack; you do not need to be an expert in every language listed.

- Experience developing software that interacts with real hardware, devices or physical systems.

- Experience taking software beyond prototypes into tested, maintainable and deployable industrial use.

- Practical railway software lifecycle experience aligned with EN 50716:2023, including requirements traceability, configuration management and verification/validation appropriate to the required software integrity level; relevant EN 50128 / EN 50657 predecessor experience is also valuable.

- Practical embedded or industrial cybersecurity experience, including secure credentials and access, signed software updates and rollback, and handling vulnerabilities in released products.

- Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills across software, communication and hardware interfaces.

- Experience with Git and structured software-development workflows.

- A practical ownership mindset: comfortable working directly with prototypes, test equipment and deployed systems and driving technical problems through to resolution.

- Ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines and communicate technical issues clearly.

- Fluent English; German is a strong advantage.

Nice to have

- Experience with industrial Linux, embedded Linux, automation or control systems.

- MATLAB/Simulink, HIL/SIL testing, data acquisition or condition-monitoring experience.

- Working knowledge of railway cybersecurity under CLC/TS 50701:2023 and of EN IEC 62443-4-1 (secure development) and EN IEC 62443-4-2 (component security) is desirable.

- Familiarity with EN 50155 and EN 50126 for equipment integration and collaboration with Systems/RAMS.

- Experience in a regulated or safety-relevant product-development environment.

  • Competitive compensation with milestone bonus scheme and full Swiss social coverage.

jobs.title: Snr. Marketing Manager, Enterprise ABM - EMEA
jobs.description:
Snr. Marketing Manager, Enterprise ABM - EMEA

Hi, I’m Harriet, Ashby’s VP Marketing. I joined Ashby in August 2022 to lead the Marketing function. My career journey has been anything but linear starting out as a yoga teacher, working as an M&A lawyer, before finding my happy place in marketing. This is a common theme across the team, and we love to see people who have built their skills both inside and outside the marketing discipline.

Over the past ~4 years, we’ve gone from a stealth brand to the default operating system for over 5,000 of the most ambitious companies in tech, finance, and healthcare. On this journey, we’ve also amassed a marketing team of ~30 folks from across North America and Europe who are some of the brightest and most humble humans that want to ‘win’, and have fun doing so. Our culture is focused on creating a space to do lots of career-defining work with the tools, people, and focus that means minimal thrash and lots of autonomy. You can learn a little more about how we work here and why our investors are excited about us here.

For this role, we are looking for someone to lead demand generation for our enterprise segment in Europe. You will have a fantastic thought partner and US counterpart, Ben, as well as the autonomy to rethink and define the strategy and execution to fit the nuances of the different European markets. It’s ABM but not in its traditional form: we’re seeking a first-principles thinker who prioritizes meaningful engagement over generic tactics / outdated playbooks (for example, prioritizing a few key impactful moments of engagement over running a laundry list of generic tactics across digital channels).

If working with both the sales and marketing team to find and convert enterprise pipeline in a low ego, highly ambitious environment appeals, we’d love to hear from you!

What you’ll be responsible for in this role

  • Partner with Ben to define our EMEA Enterprise ABM strategy and the channels we bet on with consideration to broader global strategy and nuances of respective European markets. Here you play the critical role of orchestrator, pulling together all of the relevant marketing channels to support a delightful discovery and prospect journey and are the point person for your counterparts in Sales.

  • Research and build prospect journey maps for target accounts, and develop the messaging, content, and creative that bring them to life, with support from our PMM, content, and creative teams.

  • Work with sales and revenue operations to build target account lists that combine data signals with rep input, and own the methodology behind them — how cohorts are built, what assumptions they rest on, and how we measure whether accounts are actually moving.

  • Manage our agency partners, including our gifting agency, Wildcard, to get campaigns executed well and fast.

  • Execute on the strategy you define which will include activities like working with your events counterpart on the coordination of dinners, activations, ancillary conference events, and stunts.

  • Apply our experimentation framework to run short sprints, learn quickly what works, and localise content, creative, and campaign strategy for EMEA markets.

You will probably love this role if:

  • You enjoy combining data and creative thinking — and you have taste. You can tell the difference between messaging that's genuinely compelling and messaging that's generic or cheesy.

  • You're prospect-obsessed. You can step into the seat of the personas you're marketing to and build campaigns that meet them where they are, at the right time, with the right message.

  • You are deeply curious and not afraid to break from traditional ABM playbooks.

  • You build trust across functions. Sales managers and reps are excited to work with you, and the marketing team is fully bought into your campaign ideas and asks.

  • You understand (and leverage) the massive advantage AI creates but not so pilled that you let efficiency gains undercut creativity and taste.

This role is not for you if:

  • You'd rely solely on 6sense (or equivalent) as your only source of truth.

  • You're strong on one half of the job but not the other. You need to move comfortably between building and interpreting dashboards, and writing compelling copy and developing creative with our gifting agency and creative teams.

  • You lean heavily on existing playbooks and tactics rather than stepping back and thinking from first principles. A lot of how we market at Ashby is deliberately different; curiosity and adaptability are critical.

  • You aren't able to operate with autonomy and run strategies end-to-end. We give clear ownership and trust you with it; you should be proactive and resourceful.

  • You believe that EMEA is one homogeneous market

Interview Plan

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via project working sessions. Our interview process is five rounds:

  1. 30-minute intro call with Michelle (Recruiting).

  2. 45-minute interview with Harriet (Hiring Manager).

  3. 45-minute interview with Ben (US lead on ABM).

  4. A take-home assignment, which you’ll have 40 mins to discuss with the hiring team.

  5. A virtual on-site of 1.5 hours with a panel of interviewers.

    • Nhi (Strategic Projects Lead)

    • Casper (Head of ENT Sales, EMEA)

    • Antonio (AI & Automations Lead, Demand Gen)

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it .

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

Senior Software Engineer

Who are we?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to own a feature area within our Product Engineering team. You'll be the engineer your product manager turns to for "is this possible, and how big is it", leading technical design for your area and seeing it through to production. You'll shape how your squad builds, mentor the engineers around you, and have real influence over what we ship for customers who depend on us to understand their cyber risk.

You'll join one of our 11 (and growing) Product Engineering squads, most of which have a product manager, designer and technical lead alongside the engineers.

Our stack is React and TypeScript on the front end, Go services with Postgres as our primary database, running on Kubernetes via Google Cloud Platform.

Our engineers work with agentic coding tools, mostly Claude Code and Cursor, and a growing part of the product is LLM-backed. You'll work this way from day one, and we'll want your ideas on what to automate next, from how we write code to how we test, review, ship and run it.

What you'll do

  • Own a feature area end to end, from design conversations with product through to production and follow-up

  • Lead technical design for your area and drive the architectural decisions within it

  • Work with product and design to shape what we build: what's possible, what it costs, and what should come first

  • Mentor the engineers around you and lift the quality of the squad's code and decisions

  • Improve the reliability, scalability and performance of the systems you own

  • Go deep on the cybersecurity domain and bring that understanding into what we build

What we're looking for

  • Typically 5+ years of relevant engineering experience at tech-centric, product-driven companies

  • Strong TypeScript and React

  • A backend language you're productive in (we use Go)

  • Solid relational database skills (we use Postgres)

  • AI coding tools as your default workflow, and the judgment to review and own what they produce

  • Pragmatic trade-offs: you weigh technical quality against what the business needs now

  • Low ego, high care: you're in it for the product and the customer, not just the code

  • A track record of leading technical design for a feature area and seeing it through to production

  • Experience mentoring engineers and lifting the quality of the code and decisions around you

What will give you an edge?

  • Cybersecurity experience

  • Running services on Kubernetes, ideally on GCP

  • Building complex applications or systems from the ground up with a cross-functional team

  • Owning a service in production: on-call, observability, and the judgment to know what to fix now and what can wait

What's in it for you?

We're fully remote, and we'd rather spend on things people actually use than on perks that look good in a job ad.

  • Stock options: every engineer gets equity, so you share in UpGuard's growth.

  • Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.

  • 18 weeks paid Parental Leave: irrespective of parenting role (all regions)

  • Personal Leave allowance: this includes sick and carer’s leave.

  • $[amount] monthly lifestyle subsidy for your financial, physical and mental wellbeing.

  • US$1,500 annual learning and development allowance, spent on whatever helps your career, not just courses.

  • WFH set-up allowance to get your home office right in your first three months.

We help security teams reduce their human attack surface by continuously monitoring and removing exposed personal data (PII) from the open web — the very data threat actors use to launch social engineering, phishing, Gen-AI deepfake, doxxing campaigns, physical threats, and identity fraud.

DeleteMe acts as a scalable, managed defense layer for your most vulnerable attack vector: your people. That’s why 30% of the Fortune 100, top tech firms, major banks, federal agencies, and U.S. states rely on DeleteMe to protect their workforce.

You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to create high-impact lifecycle touchpoints, tackle churn with precision, and ensure that our messaging not only reaches the inbox—but drives action.

jobs.title: Senior Media Consultant (Mensch)
Lead R&D Engineer, Tritium-Breeding Blanket
jobs.description:
Lead R&D Engineer, Tritium-Breeding Blanket

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

TEAM AND ROLE

  • Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

  • Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

As Lead R&D Engineer for the Stellaris tritium-breeding blanket, you will build and lead Proxima Fusion’s blanket development from initial concept to first prototype tests. You will translate a defined R&D budget into a small set of parallel breeder-blanket concepts, developed rapidly with external research and industrial partners.

Remote maintainability is a fundamental part of the blanket architecture from day one. Each concept must be thought with the power plant architecture in mind and demonstrate how blanket modules can be installed, connected, inspected, replaced and recovered remotely.

The objective is to leverage existing public research, challenge the most consequential assumptions, learn from hardware quickly and iterate to a functional blanket concept for our future commercial plant fleet.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Own the blanket design from initial requirements through conceptual design, prototype manufacture and testing, with accountability for budget, schedule and technical outcomes.

  • Own the integrated remote-maintenance architecture for each concept, including segmentation, access, handling, service connections, inspection, replacement and recovery from failed operations.

  • Own the compliance analysis across neutronics, thermal hydraulics, structural integrity, materials, tritium, decommissioning, safety and remote maintenance.

  • Own the rapid fail-fast prototype: select what to test and lead its design, procurement, manufacture, instrumentation, commissioning and test campaign on ambitious timelines.

  • Own the translation of test results into updated models, requirements, risk assessments and design decisions.

  • Own and build the multidisciplinary, technical design team.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A Master’s degree or higher in mechanical engineering, nuclear engineering, materials science, chemical engineering, physics or equivalent experience.

  • Have led the development of complex nuclear, thermal, chemical or energy technology from conceptual design into hardware and testing, under budget and time constraints.

  • Able to lead multidisciplinary trade studies without converging prematurely on a preferred solution.

  • Strong knowledge in several relevant domains, such as thermal hydraulics, structural mechanics, neutronics, nuclear materials, tritium systems, high-temperature coolants, corrosion, manufacturing or remote handling.

  • Able to distinguish between analysis that enables a decision and analysis that merely adds detail.

  • Comfortable structuring and managing technical work with external institutes, industrial partners and specialist suppliers.

  • Willing to test critical assumptions early, learn from failure and stop weak development paths.

  • Able to make clear and defensible engineering decisions under uncertainty.

  • Experience with fusion blankets, fission-reactor components, breeder materials, tritium systems or remotely maintained nuclear equipment are an advantage, but are explicitly not necessary.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

Customer Success Manager

We're looking for a Customer Success Manager to join our growing CS team in London, reporting to our Chief of Staff. You'll own a portfolio of clients — including hedge funds, oil majors, refiners, vessel owners and trading companies — and be responsible for their onboarding, adoption, retention and growth. As part of a small, global CS team, there's plenty of room to shape the role and grow with it.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own onboarding, training and support for your client portfolio, driving product adoption and account health.

  • Build strong relationships with clients, understanding their workflows and challenges.

  • Partner with Sales to spot cross-sell and upsell opportunities, and manage renewal risk.

  • Feed client insight back to the Product team to help shape the roadmap.

  • Maintain and improve our Customer Success processes and tools.

  • Help build a company-wide culture centered on customer success.



About You

  • Some knowledge of, or experience in, oil & gas, commodities, or trading — you understand the world our clients operate in.

  • Experience in a customer-facing role such as Customer Success or Account Management — ideally supporting a data, intelligence, or SaaS product.

  • Comfortable using AI and automation tools in your day-to-day work, and curious to find smarter ways of doing things.

  • Strong communicator, comfortable building relationships and influencing stakeholders.

  • Analytical and process-minded — you like understanding what drives client value.

  • Proactive and comfortable with ambiguity — happy to figure things out and get stuck in.

  • High level of integrity and alignment with Sparta's values.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

jobs.title: Platform Architect - Banking
jobs.description:
Platform Architect - Banking

About us

EggAI is a fast-growing AI consulting and development startup. We build agentic AI solutions for enterprise clients. We are growing in several European markets.

The role

You will own the design of a shared AI platform for our clients. The platform has two parts. An AI Control Plane governs what agents may do, through identity and delegated permissions, policy enforcement, approvals, budgets and durable audit records. A managed AI Runtime is where the agents run. Both integrate with the client's identity, security, delivery and audit services.

You will set the architecture, define how services and controls fit together, and make sure what the team builds is sound, assured and ready for production. The role reaches across engineering, security, audit, risk and the client's architecture function. You will take designs through their governance, record the decisions, and give the engineers a design they can build and the client a design they can approve.

You will be EggAI's accountable architecture lead on the engagement, leading design for a delivery team of platform engineers. You make the technical decisions within the team's remit, recommend on the rest, and secure the client's approval where their architecture or risk governance requires it. 

What you will do

- Own the architecture of the AI Control Plane and AI Runtime and keep it aligned with the client's architecture standards, cloud substrate, API gateway, identity provider and audit services.
- Define service interfaces and contracts. Decide where each security and policy control is enforced: in the gateway, the control plane, the runtime or the client's own services.
- Keep the design record. Write architecture decision records (ADRs) and record every deviation from the client's standards or our reference designs for a client decision.
- Take designs through the client's architecture and risk forums. Secure approvals in time for dependent work, so that design precedes implementation.
- Lead design and quality review across all platform services. Review engineers' changes, cross-service tests and fault exercises with the CTO.
- Define how the architecture will be proven. Agree acceptance criteria with engineers and client control owners for each interface, control and infrastructure contract, including behaviour when a dependency fails, and review the test evidence showing they are met.
- Hold the build to the design's principles: policy enforced outside the agent, decisions recorded before actions take effect, fail closed with stop always available, and audit evidence that is administered independently of the people who build and run the platform, reconciled against what actually happened, and readable with the client's own tools.
- Maintain the inventory of platform controls. Record for each one whether it is enforced or only monitored, whether it is implemented, tested or still open, and what evidence it produces, so acceptance reviews work from a current record and coverage gaps are visible.
- Assess proposed technology, scope and dependency changes for their effect on the design, controls, effort and running costs, and give the programme lead a clear basis for plan and cost decisions.
- Evaluate new runtimes and managed services against the platform's control requirements. Compare shared controls with provider-native ones on integration effort, operating cost and assurance gaps, separate what is verified from what is assumed, and recommend whether to adopt, change the design or hold scope.
- Lead the technical assessment of production readiness. Review recovery, containment and fault-exercise evidence, and give the programme lead a clear view of what is ready and what is not.
- Stay with the platform through go-live and the support period after it. Resolve the architectural issues that production exposes, and decide when a fix is a design change rather than a defect.
- Prepare the client's receiving engineers to maintain the design. Lead the architecture parts of training and handover, and leave documentation, decision records and guidance they can extend without you.

Essential experience

- You have been the accountable solution or platform architect for systems that went into production, and have led engineers through building them.
- You have delivered cloud platforms into production in a regulated environment and taken designs through formal architecture and risk governance.
- You know a major cloud platform in depth: networking, identity, secrets, Kubernetes and managed services. Azure is strongly preferred.
- You have hands-on experience with API gateways, identity and delegation using OAuth and OIDC, and policy as code.
- You work with infrastructure as code, GitOps and software supply-chain controls, and understand how they underpin reproducible environments, conformance tests and release assurance.
- You have designed systems that must produce audit evidence and fail safely: durable records, immutable storage, separation of duties and deny-by-default access. You have sound judgement about retries, partial failure, idempotency, identity propagation and recovery.
- You write clear architecture decision records and can explain and defend a design to senior architects, risk owners and engineers.

Nice to have

- Delivery in financial services or banking.
- LLM or agent platforms in production, including model gateways, agent orchestration and protocols such as MCP and A2A.
- Audit, evidence retention or AI risk controls, including EU AI Act, PRA or FCA expectations.
- Products in this space such as Kong, Open Policy Agent or Microsoft Foundry.

Practical details

- Hybrid working and client-site attendance will depend on the engagement.
- You will need to complete the background and security checks required by the client.

jobs.title: Scientific Product Manager
jobs.description:
Scientific Product Manager

About CuspAI

CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering.

We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock.

We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters.

We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us.

The Role

Due to rapid growth in our partner lab network, we are seeking a Scientific Product Manager to join our Product team and bring partner labs and their experimental workflows onto the CuspAI platform.

Your impact

This is an exciting opportunity to join the product team at CuspAI, working closely with materials scientists, ML researchers and platform engineers to make AI-driven experimentation work in real laboratories. As one of a small team of Scientific Product Managers, you will take ownership of a set of partner labs and the lab integration work around them, translating what each lab actually needs into requirements our engineers and ML researchers can build against. Alongside the product work, you will spend real time with your partners' teams and their experimental data.

What You Will Do

Product Requirements & Roadmap

  • Shape and prioritise the roadmap for how experimental data, protocols and campaigns get into the CuspAI platform, together with your fellow Scientific Product Managers, the engineering lead and the wider product team.

  • Write requirements, specifications and acceptance criteria that engineers can build from, covering experiment types, instrument integrations and LIMS/ELN connections, and work with the data team on the underlying data models and provenance.

  • Contribute to decisions on what we build, what we integrate, and what we leave to partners' existing systems.

Partner Lab Onboarding

  • Lead technical discovery with the partner labs you take on: map their workflows, instruments, sample logic and data systems, and pin down the true experimental unit and the parameters that matter.

  • Own onboarding for your partner labs from scoping to the first closed-loop campaign, and turn each onboarding into reusable patterns and documentation shared across the team so the next one is faster.

  • Act as the main scientific counterpart for the partner labs you look after, and represent the product in partner meetings, workshops and conferences.

Closed-Loop Campaigns

  • Work with ML researchers to design optimisation campaigns (e.g. Bayesian optimisation) that respect real experimental constraints such as throughput, noise and failed samples.

  • Define how platform-driven campaigns are validated, including benchmarks against manual or legacy workflows, success metrics and the evidence we bring to partners.

Must Have Skills and Qualifications:

  • PhD in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Chemical Engineering or a related experimental discipline, or equivalent experience in scientific research.

  • Hands-on experience with high-throughput or automated experimentation (e.g. robotic synthesis, combinatorial libraries, automated characterisation, or self-driving / closed-loop labs) in industry, a national lab or research institute, or academia.

  • Proven track record of translating scientific or process needs into requirements for engineers, software teams or automation vendors, and of validating that what was built works in the lab.

  • Firsthand understanding of how experimental data is produced and where it fails: which metadata and provenance matter, instrument quirks, data quality issues, and what makes a dataset usable for machine learning.

  • Depth in at least one materials domain (e.g. semiconductors and thin films including photovoltaics, catalysis and electrochemistry, energy materials including batteries, polymers and formulations, or separations and surfaces) and the curiosity to work across others.

  • Working knowledge of Python for data handling and analysis; comfortable working with APIs and data schemas.

  • Strong communicator and a proven collaborator, comfortable working directly with external partner labs as well as multidisciplinary science, ML, product and engineering teams.

Bonus Points (But Not Critical):

  • Direct experience with closed-loop optimisation in an automated setting, such as Bayesian optimisation, active learning or design of experiments.

  • Experience with research data management, LIMS/ELN systems, FAIR data or metadata schemas, and familiarity with lab data standards (e.g. SiLA 2, AnIML, Allotrope).

  • Instrument integration experience, including vendor software, data formats, and scheduling or orchestration.

  • Product or project management experience, such as roadmaps, user research, external research collaborations or vendor relationships. We are equally open to strong experimental scientists making their first move into product.

  • Experience working in industry at a materials, chemicals, energy or deep-tech company, or closely with industry at a research institution or national lab.

  • Experience coordinating work across multiple labs, sites or countries.

Additional Considerations

This role could be based in any of our locations with the expectation of being in the office three days per week. Additionally, there may be regular travel required to partner labs and other locations for collaboration and project work.

What We Offer

  • A competitive salary: We value and reward impact and growth

  • Equity in CuspAI: You have a stake in the success of the company

  • Time off to stay fresh: 28 days holiday (DE, NL, UK) or 21 days holiday (JP, SG, US), in addition to local public holidays

  • ‘Gold Standard’ parental leave: 26 weeks (primary caregiver) and 12 weeks (secondary caregiver) at full pay - we look after you and your family while we work on the most important materials discovery problems together

  • Professional development budget: We invest in your career development so you can stay up to date with the latest industry knowledge or add to your skills to increase impact and growth

  • Solve meaningful problems: See how your work has a direct impact on advancing materials science and solving sustainability and climate-related problems through the creation and application of bleeding-edge SOTA technology and revolutionary techniques

  • True interdisciplinary teamwork: Be part of a deeply collaborative environment bridging AI research, computational chemistry, and experimental science - work with world-class researchers and engineers who enjoy sharing knowledge and supporting each other


Join us in shaping the future of materials with AI. Together, we can create groundbreaking solutions for a more sustainable world.


CuspAI is an equal opportunities employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), veteran status, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

We actively encourage applications from all backgrounds and value the unique perspectives and contributions that diversity brings to our team.

Please let us know if you require any specific adjustments during or after the interview process. We will do everything we can within reason to accommodate.

This is not a support or reporting role. You will be trusted to make decisions, own results, and directly influence the growth of the business.


This role is strictly for candidates with in-house e-commerce experience. Applicants whose primary Google Ads experience comes from agencies, consultancies, or freelance work will not be considered.

We are looking for people who have owned performance outcomes within an e-commerce business, where success is measured by revenue, profitability, customer acquisition, and long-term growth rather than client management and campaign delivery. You should have experience working directly within a commercial business and feel comfortable taking responsibility for results, beyond simply providing recommendations.

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience managing Google Ads campaigns

  • Proven hands-on experience managing Google Ads for an e-commerce business, with direct responsibility for performance and profitability

  • Strong experience with Search, Shopping, and Performance Max campaigns

  • Proven experience working as part of an in-house e-commerce team rather than as an agency, consultant, or freelancer

  • Strong understanding of attribution, tracking, and performance measurement

  • Familiarity with Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, and Google Merchant Center

  • Highly analytical with strong attention to detail

  • Fluent in English, both written and spoken

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with changing priorities

  • Curious, proactive, and focused on continuous improvement

  • Able to take ownership and make decisions independently

  • We are actively pushing AI and automation across the business, so you need to be comfortable working in that direction and not resistant to change

  • Senior, but practical

  • Data-driven without becoming overly theoretical

  • Comfortable taking ownership and making decisions

  • Naturally curious and always looking for performance improvements

  • Focused on outcomes rather than activity

  • Able to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution

  • Motivated by building and scaling rather than simply maintaining campaigns

  • Available to start immediately / ASAP

We are investing in strengthening our presence there and expect it to become an increasingly important location for our team over time. Our wider team works across London, Belgrade, Barcelona, Frankfurt, Oxfordshire, Istanbul, and Guangzhou.

The role involves travel approximately every 4-8 weeks to Belgrade, Barcelona, London, or other team locations for planning sessions, workshops, team gatherings, and strategic discussions. While most work takes place remotely, we value spending time together in person, particularly as the company continues to scale.

This is a long-term opportunity for someone who wants to make a meaningful contribution to scaling an international e-commerce business over the coming years.

In Our Culture at ennovationHUB, We Value:

  • Accountability over excuses

  • Execution over talk

  • Clarity over politics

  • Learning through doing

We welcome people from diverse backgrounds. What matters most is the quality of your work, taking ownership, and helping the business move forward.

Back in 2012, we were a group of engineers and designers who decided we wanted to build things—so we did. Today, our builder mindset is driving us to become an AI-native organization across every function. We’re still evolving, and that’s part of the opportunity. This position is 100% remote within LatAm.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Technical Leadership: you will lead technical conversations, be hands-on in building applications or proofs of concepts, and establish AI/ML guidelines and standards for our partners, prospects, and across the organization.

Required Skills & Experience

  • 12+ years building AI/ML systems, with production experience shipping and operating them
  • Fluency with the modern LLM stack: frontier models, RAG, vector databases, agentic frameworks, and the evals and guardrails that make them trustworthy in production

Nice to Have

jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)

Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their
logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

  • Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
    technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
  • User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
    partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
  • API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
  • Payments and billing.
  • ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,
    observability and alerting, consent and retention.
  • The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on
    Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access.
  • Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were
    never designed to meet.

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want
someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and
used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and
Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity
layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How we work

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around
agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,
the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the
implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What
we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand:
knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not
move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a
week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that
an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for
how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at
least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a
green build is never on its own enough to merge.

Requirements

You'll thrive here if you have…

  • Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to
    the machine they run on.
  • A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a
    migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for.
  • Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you
    will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's.
  • React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data
    loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters.
  • TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types
    are carrying real weight.
  • Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to
    pick up Pulumi.
  • Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but
    debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into.
  • Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema
    change does under load.
  • Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have
    opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a
    colleague's.
  • Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and
    patience for other people's undocumented edge cases.
  • A working day that overlaps ours: based within CET ±3.
  • Fluent in English, our working language.

Nice to have

  • Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX.
  • Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR
    beyond a cookie banner.
  • Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations.
  • Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent.
  • Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry.
  • Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU
    ETS..).

Benefits

As part of our team, you will:

  • 🌱 Have a chance to re-shape the future of climate in the logistics.
  • 👩‍💻 Be empowered to deliver your best work remotely, and get a stipend to set
    you up.
  • 🏄‍♂️ Have a flat hierarchy, where you will have direct access to the founders
    and won't be tied up in politics.
  • 🎓 Have a high degree of learning and ownership in a dynamic environment.
  • 🏝 Take part in our team-building events.
